<b>Доли коры.</b> Центральная (Роландова: Cortical lobes. The central (Rolandic) sulcus separates the frontal lobe (red) from the parietal lobe (blue); the lateral (Sylvian) sulcus sets off the temporal lobe (green), and the parieto-occipital sulcus the occipital lobe (yellow). The limbic lobe (pink) is visible on the medial surface: cingulate gyrus, hippocampus, olfactory cortex. The small insular lobe is hidden at the bottom of the lateral sulcus. Primary sulci appear from the 5th month; tertiary sulci (individual, like fingerprints) by the end of the 7th.
<b>Поля Бродмана.</b> В 1909 году Корбин: Brodmann areas. In 1909 Korbinian Brodmann used Nissl staining to divide the cortex into 52 cytoarchitectonic areas. Primary areas (3, 4, 17, 41) receive input directly from the thalamic relay nuclei and have a precise topographic map; secondary areas (1, 2, 6, 18, 19, 42) assemble features into images; tertiary (association) areas combine streams from different senses. Click an area.
<b>Шесть слоёв новой коры.</b> 3/4 нейро: Six layers of the neocortex. 3/4 of cortical neurons are pyramidal cells. The granular layers II and IV are the input (from other cortical areas and from the thalamus), the pyramidal layers III and V are the output (III to other areas and across the corpus callosum, V to the striatum, brainstem and spinal cord), and layers I and VI handle integration; the nonspecific thalamic nuclei project here. Red is a giant Betz cell; purple are spindle-shaped (fusiform) neurons.
<b>Латерализация.</b> Левое полушарие: а: Lateralization. Left hemisphere: analysis of the right visual field, touch with the right hand, vocabulary and semantics of speech, writing, full-fledged speech. Right: the left visual field, touch with the left hand, the emotional tone of speech, spatial imagination, music. The hemispheres constantly exchange signals through the corpus callosum (blue streams). Dividing functions pays off: less time is spent on transmission.
<b>Расщеплённый мозг.</b> В 1970-е годы,: Split brain. In the 1970s, to relieve severe epileptic seizures, surgeons cut patients’ corpus callosum. Michael Gazzaniga found that the hemispheres then work almost independently: an object shown in the left visual field (right hemisphere) is recognized but cannot be named, because speech is in the left. Later the idea of a strict division of functions was softened.
<b>Путь сигнала через колонку.</b> Волок: Signal path through a column. A fiber from the thalamus (yellow) arrives in layer IV → stellate cells pass the signal to layer III pyramidal cells → layer III sends it to other cortical areas and across the corpus callosum (blue) and excites a Betz cell in layer V → its axon leaves the cortex downward into the pyramidal tract.
<b>Колонка.</b> Вернон Маунткасл погружа: Column. Vernon Mountcastle advanced an electrode vertically through a cat’s somatosensory cortex — and every cell he encountered responded to the same stimulus. A column runs through all six layers and works as a separate processor. In the primary visual cortex, neighboring minicolumns respond to lines of different orientations.
Впереди центральной борозды. Задняя част: In front of the central sulcus. Its posterior part is the motor cortex (area 4) and premotor cortex (6); below lies Broca’s area; in front, the prefrontal cortex: plans and decisions.
Между центральной и теменно-затылочной б: Between the central and parieto-occipital sulci. The anterior part handles skin, muscle and pain sensation (areas 3, 1, 2); the posterior part is the parietal association cortex.
Ниже боковой борозды. Слуховая кора (41,: Below the lateral sulcus. Auditory cortex (41, 42), Wernicke’s area (22), object recognition; deep inside lie the hippocampus and amygdala.
Позади теменно-затылочной борозды. Зрите: Behind the parieto-occipital sulcus. Visual cortex: primary area 17 along the banks of the calcarine sulcus, secondary areas 18 and 19.
На медиальной стороне, окружает место от: On the medial surface, encircling the place where the hemisphere joins the diencephalon: the cingulate and parahippocampal gyri, hippocampus, olfactory cortex. Emotion and memory.
Пять долей, 52 поля Бродмана, шесть слоё: Five lobes, 52 Brodmann areas, six layers and processor columns. See where the cortex speaks, sees and moves, and how a signal passes through its layers.
\n <div><h2>Борозды и извилины</h2>:
Sulci and gyri

The primary sulci (central, lateral, parieto-occipital) appear from the 5th month of fetal development and are present in everyone. Secondary sulci come later. Tertiary sulci produce fine furrowing, and their pattern is individual.

Cortical areas are not equal

Primary areas are the cortical stations of the sensory systems, with direct input from the thalamic relay nuclei and a precise topographic map. Secondary areas lie next to the primary ones, are connected with the association nuclei and assemble features into images. Tertiary areas — the inferior parietal lobule and the occipito-temporo-parietal region — combine different streams.

In sensory systems an image is assembled from elements; in motor systems the flow runs the other way: overall program (prefrontal cortex) → individual movements (6, 8) → signals to the muscles (4).

Cortical cells

  • Pyramidal cells — 3/4 of cortical neurons, with many dendritic spines (a sign of learning).
  • Betz cells — the largest neurons in the brain (V. A. Betz, 1874), in layer V of the precentral gyrus; their axons go into the pyramidal tract.
  • Von Economo neurons — large spindle-shaped cells found only in humans, great apes, elephants and cetaceans: fast communication between the frontal, parietal and cingulate cortex.
  • Long-axon Golgi type I cells project beyond the cortex; short-axon Golgi type II cells form local networks.

  • Area boundaries on the model are simplified and follow the classical map.
  • Layer thickness and cell size in the column are exaggerated.

<b>Гиппокамп</b> («морской конёк», описа: Hippocampus (“seahorse”, described by Giulio Aranzi in the 16th century) — the key structure of the archicortex, lying deep in the temporal lobe on the floor of the inferior horn of the lateral ventricle. Memory of the current day, spatial learning, a “catalog” of long-term memory. It retains the capacity for neurogenesis and can grow with training: it is enlarged in taxi drivers and waiters.
<b>Свод</b> — пучок белого вещества, вых: Fornix — a bundle of white matter leaving the hippocampus. It arches around the thalamus toward the caudate nucleus, runs along the wall of the third ventricle and ends in the mammillary bodies.
<b>Мамиллярные тела</b> — выступы на ниж: Mammillary bodies — bulges on the underside of the diencephalon. From them the mammillothalamic tract runs to the anterior thalamic nuclei.
<b>Передние ядра таламуса</b> — лимбичес: Anterior thalamic nuclei — the limbic part of the thalamus; they relay the Papez circuit signal to the cingulate gyrus.
<b>Поясная извилина</b> лежит над мозоли: The cingulate gyrus lies above the corpus callosum. Through it the hippocampus is connected with many regions of the neocortex; its areas 24–26 detect mismatches and errors.
<b>Парагиппокампальная извилина и энтори: Parahippocampal gyrus and entorhinal cortex — the entrance to the hippocampus: the perforant path to the dentate gyrus starts here. The circuit closes.
<b>Миндалина</b> — у переднего конца гип: Amygdala — at the front end of the hippocampus. It gives memories their emotional coloring.
<b>Древняя кора (палеокортекс)</b>: обон: Paleocortex (ancient cortex): the olfactory bulbs, tracts, olfactory trigones and tubercles, the uncus of the parahippocampal gyrus. Here whole odors are assembled from individual odorant molecules. In humans the neocortex makes up almost 96% of the entire cortex.
<b>Круг Пейпеза</b> — замкнутая петля: г: Papez circuit — a closed loop: hippocampus → fornix → mammillary bodies → mammillothalamic tract → anterior thalamic nuclei → cingulate gyrus → parahippocampal (entorhinal) cortex → back to the hippocampus. The loop makes it possible to hold information and transfer it from short-term to long-term memory (NMDA receptors are at work). Click a structure or start the circuit.
<b>Сигнал идёт по кругу Пейпеза.</b> Обх: The signal travels around the Papez circuit. The loop repeats: this way information “cycles” and is held for hours — the hippocampus stores the memory of the current day until it is rewritten into neocortical networks. With bilateral hippocampal damage, almost nothing new is remembered.
<b>Поперечный срез гиппокампа</b>. Синие: Cross-section of the hippocampus. Blue triangles are pyramidal cells of Ammon’s horn (fields CA1–CA3), red dots are granule cells of the dentate gyrus. The trisynaptic loop: perforant path (green) from the entorhinal cortex → dentate granule cells → mossy fibers (orange) → CA3 pyramidal cells → Schaffer collaterals (yellow) → CA1 pyramidal cells → subiculum and entorhinal cortex (purple). Click “Stimulus”.
<b>Одиночный стимул.</b> Залп проходит т: Single stimulus. A volley passes through three synapses in a row. On the right is the excitatory postsynaptic potential (EPSP) in CA1: this is how strongly CA1 responds before learning. Now apply “Tetanus”.
<b>Тетанус</b> — короткая серия частых з: Tetanus — a short burst of high-frequency volleys. CA1 pyramidal cells depolarize strongly, NMDA receptors open, calcium enters the spines — the Schaffer synapses are strengthened (the yellow boutons grow). This is long-term potentiation, the cellular basis of memory. Apply another single stimulus.
<b>После ДВП</b> тот же одиночный стимул: After LTP the same single stimulus evokes a noticeably larger response in CA1: the synapse has “remembered” the training. This is how maps of familiar places and the events of the day are written into the hippocampus.
Гиппокамп держит память текущего дня: си: The hippocampus holds the memory of the current day: the signal runs around the Papez circuit and the trisynaptic loop, and high-frequency stimulation strengthens synapses — this is how memory is born.
\n <div><h2>Три вида коры</h2>\n:
Three kinds of cortex

Neocortex — almost 96% of the cortex in humans, six layers. Paleocortex (ancient cortex) — the olfactory brain: bulbs, tracts, olfactory trigones and tubercles, the periamygdaloid area. Archicortex (old cortex) — the hippocampus, dentate gyrus, subiculum, part of the cingulate and parahippocampal gyri.

Spatial memory

In rats learning a maze, its layout is literally “written” into the hippocampus. Thanks to the hippocampus, a person steps around a pothole on an unfamiliar road: as they move, the hippocampus retrieves knowledge from long-term memory and corrects the route.

What is accurate here

  • The position of the hippocampus in the temporal lobe, the fornix around the thalamus, the mammillary bodies.
  • The order of the links in the Papez circuit.
  • The trisynaptic loop and long-term potentiation in CA1.

Simplifications

  • Structures are simplified; the circuit is shown for one hemisphere.
  • The LTP time scale is compressed: in real life potentiation lasts hours and days.

<b>Древний мозжечок</b> — клочок и узело: Archicerebellum — the flocculus and nodulus together with the fastigial nuclei. It tunes innate balance reflexes (taking vestibular information into account) and eye movements.
<b>Старый мозжечок</b> — кора червя и ме: Paleocerebellum — the cortex of the vermis and the medial part of the hemispheres together with the interposed (globose and emboliform) nuclei. It automates locomotion — moving through space. It receives muscle and skin sensation via the spinocerebellar tracts and controls the extrapyramidal system.
<b>Новый мозжечок</b> — латеральные част: Neocerebellum — the lateral parts of the hemispheres and the dentate nuclei. Programs that arose in the motor and premotor cortex (areas 4, 6, 8) are gradually “rewritten” here: fine finger movements, speech, facial expressions. Corrections travel back to area 4 through the ventral lateral nucleus of the thalamus.
<b>Ядро шатра</b> — самое медиальное, ра: Fastigial nucleus — the most medial; it works with the archicerebellum: balance and eye movements. Its efferents run through the inferior peduncles to the vestibular nuclei and the reticular formation.
<b>Шаровидные ядра</b> (5) вместе с проб: Globose nuclei (5) together with the emboliform nucleus form the interposed nucleus — in chimpanzees it is still a single one. They work with the paleocerebellum: locomotion.
<b>Пробковидное ядро</b> (6) — часть про: Emboliform nucleus (6) — part of the interposed nucleus. Through the superior peduncles it influences the red nucleus of the midbrain.
<b>Зубчатое ядро</b> (7) — самое крупное: Dentate nucleus (7) — the largest, a folded “pouch” with its hilum open medially. It works with the neocerebellum; its output goes to the thalamus and cortex.
Superior peduncles — to the midbrain. Input: the anterior spinocerebellar tract. Output: from the cerebellar nuclei to the red nucleus (the main route to the extrapyramidal system) and to the thalamus, and on to the motor cortex.
<b>Средние ножки</b> — самые толстые, от: Middle peduncles — the thickest, from the pons. The cortico-ponto-cerebellar pathway: the cerebral hemispheres send “copies” of motor programs here.
<b>Нижние ножки</b> — к продолговатому м: Inferior peduncles — to the medulla oblongata. Input: from the inferior olives (movement correction), from the spinal cord, from the gracile and cuneate nuclei, the vestibular nuclei and the reticular formation. Output: from the fastigial nuclei to the vestibular nuclei.
<b>Мозжечок</b> — «малый мозг» за намёто: Cerebellum — the “little brain” beneath the tentorium cerebelli: 9–10 cm across, weighing 120–160 g, 10% of the brain’s volume but more than half of all its neurons. The vermis is in the middle, with two hemispheres at the sides; folia increase the cortical area. Colors show the functional parts: archicerebellum (flocculus and nodulus), paleocerebellum (vermis and medial zones), neocerebellum (lateral hemispheres). In the first year of life the cerebellum grows faster than other parts of the brain (40 g at 3 months, 80 g at 9 months).
<b>Горизонтальный срез</b>. Как и в полу: Horizontal section. As in the cerebral hemispheres: cortex on the outside (three layers of gray matter), white matter beneath it — the “arbor vitae” (tree of life) — and nuclei deep inside. From the inside out: fastigial nucleus, globose, emboliform and the folded dentate. Click a nucleus.
<b>Кора мозжечка: три слоя.</b> Внизу <b: Cerebellar cortex: three layers. At the bottom is the granular layer — the densest layer in the brain, made of granule cells. In the middle is the ganglionic layer — the cell bodies of Purkinje cells. At the top is the molecular layer: the flat dendritic fans of Purkinje cells stand in a single plane, and parallel fibers (granule cell axons with T-shaped branching) pierce them crosswise — an orthogonal lattice. Purkinje cells are inhibitory: they constantly restrain the cerebellar nuclei (light-blue sparks heading down).
<b>Моховидные волокна</b> (зелёные) несу: Mossy fibers (green) carry signals from the pons, spinal cord and vestibular nuclei to granule cells → granule cells excite a bundle of parallel fibers → the Purkinje cells under the bundle are excited and inhibit their nucleus more strongly. At the same time stellate and basket (GABA) cells inhibit neighboring Purkinje cells — a hole opens in the “inhibitory curtain”, and the nucleus beneath it (orange) launches a movement.
<b>Лазящее волокно</b> (фиолетовое) прих: Climbing fiber (purple) comes from the inferior olive and wraps around a single Purkinje cell, which fires a powerful complex spike. This is the signal “the movement was inaccurate”. Parallel-fiber synapses that were active at the same time weaken — motor memory forms on the Purkinje dendrites.
<b>Выработка навыка.</b> Каждая проба —: Learning a skill. Each trial combines the context of the movement (mossy fibers) and an error signal (climbing fiber). The yellow synapses of the bundle fade, the Purkinje cells under the bundle inhibit the nucleus less — and it issues a more accurate command. On the right, the error falls from trial to trial.
<b>Навык выработан.</b> Мозжечок запомни: Skill acquired. The cerebellum has memorized how to perform this movement quickly and accurately. The basal ganglia assemble such individual movements into a long program — the whole dance — while the cerebellum is responsible for each step.
к таламусу и красному ядру: to the thalamus and red nucleus
Больше половины нейронов мозга — в мозже: More than half of the brain’s neurons are in the cerebellum. Motor memory is written onto the dendrites of Purkinje cells: how to make each movement quickly and accurately.
\n <div><h2>Доли и дольки</h2>\n:
Lobes and lobules

The deepest fissures divide the cerebellum into the anterior, posterior and flocculonodular lobes. Lobules of the vermis: lingula, central lobule, culmen, declive, folium, tuber, pyramis, uvula, nodulus. Lobules of the hemispheres: ala of the central lobule, quadrangular, semilunar and biventral lobules, tonsil, flocculus.

Inputs

Vestibular information from the nuclei of cranial nerve VIII, the spinocerebellar tracts and the pontine nuclei, which relay signals from the frontal cortex.

What is accurate here

  • The vermis, hemispheres, flocculus, three pairs of peduncles.
  • Four nuclei and their order from the midline outward.
  • The orthogonal lattice: Purkinje fans and parallel fibers, mossy and climbing inputs, basket and stellate cells.

  • The shape of the cerebellum is simplified, with fewer folia than in reality.
  • The circuit shows 9 Purkinje cells instead of millions.

<b>Правое предсердие</b> принимает веноз: The right atrium receives venous blood from the whole body via the superior and inferior venae cavae. Its wall contains the sinoatrial node, the heart’s pacemaker.
<b>Правый желудочек</b> через лёгочный с: The right ventricle pumps oxygen-poor blood through the pulmonary trunk to the lungs — the pulmonary circulation. Pressure here is low (about 25 mmHg), so the wall is thin, 3–5 mm.
<b>Левое предсердие</b> принимает насыще: The left atrium receives oxygen-rich blood from the lungs via the four pulmonary veins.
<b>Левый желудочек</b> выбрасывает кровь: The left ventricle ejects blood into the aorta — the systemic circulation. Pressure reaches 120 mmHg; the wall is the thickest, 10–15 mm.
<b>Клапаны</b> пропускают кровь только в: Valves let blood flow in one direction only. Between the atria and ventricles are the tricuspid valve (right) and the bicuspid, or mitral, valve (left); their cusps are held by the chordae tendineae. At the outlets are the semilunar valves of the pulmonary trunk and aorta. The valves snapping shut produce the heart sounds, “lub-dub”.
<b>Крупные сосуды.</b> Аорта (из левого: Great vessels. The aorta (from the left ventricle) is the largest artery, about 2.5 cm in diameter. The pulmonary trunk divides into the right and left pulmonary arteries. The superior and inferior venae cavae empty into the right atrium, and the four pulmonary veins into the left.
<b>Венечные (коронарные) артерии</b> отх: The coronary arteries arise from the very beginning of the aorta and supply the heart muscle. Their blockage by a clot is a myocardial infarction: the patch of muscle deprived of oxygen dies.
<b>Сердце</b> — мышечный насос размером: The heart is a muscular pump the size of a fist (about 300 g). It has four chambers: two atria on top and two ventricles below. The right half (blue) pumps oxygen-poor blood to the lungs, the left half (red) pumps oxygen-rich blood to the whole body. At 75 beats per minute a cycle lasts 0.8 s: atrial systole 0.1 s, ventricular systole 0.3 s, general diastole (pause) 0.4 s. Click a part of the heart.
<b>Проводящая система.</b> Сердце сокращ: Conduction system. The heart contracts on its own, without commands from the brain (automaticity). The impulse arises in the sinoatrial node (60–80 times a minute) → spreads as a wave across the atria (the P wave on the ECG) → is delayed in the atrioventricular node for 0.1 s so the atria can finish pushing blood in → through the bundle of His, its branches and the Purkinje fibers it almost instantly spreads through the ventricles (the QRS complex). The T wave is ventricular repolarization. Nerves and hormones only speed up or slow down the rhythm.
<b>Два круга кровообращения</b> (открыл: Two circulations (discovered by William Harvey, 1628). Systemic circulation: left ventricle → aorta → arteries → organ capillaries (blood gives up oxygen and becomes venous) → veins → venae cavae → right atrium. Pulmonary circulation: right ventricle → pulmonary arteries → lung capillaries (blood picks up oxygen) → pulmonary veins → left atrium. A full circuit of the blood takes about 20–25 seconds.
<b>Полная атриовентрикулярная блокада.</: Complete atrioventricular block. The impulse from the sinoatrial node does not reach the ventricles. The atria beat at their own rhythm (P waves), while the ventricles are driven by a backup pacemaker at only 35–40 beats a minute, and the QRS complexes are no longer linked to the P waves. The organs receive too little blood; the treatment is an implanted pacemaker.
Четыре камеры, четыре клапана и собствен: Four chambers, four valves and a pacemaker of its own. Over a lifetime the heart beats about 3 billion times, pumping 5 liters of blood every minute.
\n <div><h2>Как работает насос</h2>:
How the pump works

In diastole, blood from the veins flows freely through the open atrioventricular valves into the ventricles. Atrial systole pushes in the last 20–30%. In ventricular systole the pressure rises, the atrioventricular valve cusps snap shut (first heart sound, “lub”), the semilunar valves open, and blood leaves into the aorta and pulmonary trunk. When the ventricles relax, the semilunar valves close (second heart sound, “dub”).

Stroke volume and cardiac output

With each contraction, each ventricle ejects about 70 mL. At 70 beats per minute that is ~5 L/min; during exercise, up to 25–30 L/min.

Regulation

  • Sympathetic nerves and epinephrine (adrenaline) increase the rate and force of contraction.
  • The vagus nerve (parasympathetic) slows the rhythm.
  • The more the ventricle is stretched by incoming blood, the more forcefully it contracts (the Frank–Starling law).

Simplifications

  • The shape of the heart is simplified; chambers are shown as volumes of blood.
  • The circulation diagram shows the main routes, not every vessel.

  • 1–3 mode

<b>Носовая полость</b> согревает, увлажн: The nasal cavity warms, humidifies and cleans the air: hairs and mucus trap dust, and the cilia of the ciliated epithelium sweep it toward the pharynx. The nasal conchae swirl the airflow. Then the air passes through the pharynx — a crossroads with the digestive tract.
<b>Гортань</b> — хрящевая «коробка» с го: The larynx is a cartilaginous “box” housing the vocal cords. During swallowing the epiglottis closes it so that food does not enter the airway. Vibration of the closed vocal cords produces the voice.
<b>Трахея</b> (10–12 см) держится открыт: The trachea (10–12 cm) is held open by 16–20 cartilaginous half-rings. It divides into two main bronchi, and these into lobar, segmental and ever smaller bronchi: about 23 generations of branching down to the alveoli. This is the bronchial tree.
<b>Лёгкие</b> — губчатые органы в плевра: The lungs are spongy organs in the pleural sacs. The right lung is larger and has three lobes, the left has two: part of the space is taken up by the heart (the cardiac notch). Inside are about 300–500 million alveoli.
<b>Диафрагма</b> — главная дыхательная м: The diaphragm is the main breathing muscle, a dome between the thoracic and abdominal cavities. When it contracts, it flattens and descends by 1.5–7 cm, the volume of the chest increases — and air flows in. It is assisted by the external intercostal muscles, which raise the ribs.
<b>Спокойное дыхание.</b> 12–18 вдохов в: Quiet breathing. 12–18 breaths per minute, tidal volume ~500 mL. Inhalation is active (the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles contract); exhalation is passive: the elastic lungs recoil on their own.
<b>Максимальный вдох.</b> Сверх обычного: Maximal inhalation. Beyond a normal breath you can take in another ~3000 mL — the inspiratory reserve volume. The accessory muscles of the neck and chest are also recruited.
<b>Форсированный выдох.</b> Брюшные и вн: Forced exhalation. The abdominal and internal intercostal muscles push out another ~1200 mL — the expiratory reserve volume. About 1200 mL always remains in the lungs (residual volume). Maximal inhalation + maximal exhalation = vital capacity, VC ≈ 3.5–5 L.
<b>Задержка дыхания.</b> CO₂ в крови рас: Breath-holding. CO₂ in the blood rises, chemoreceptors in the medulla oblongata and the carotid arteries send an ever stronger signal to the respiratory center — and inhalation becomes unavoidable. The main stimulus for breathing is CO₂, not a lack of oxygen.
<b>Дыхательная система.</b> Воздух идёт: Respiratory system. Air travels through the nose, pharynx, larynx and trachea into the bronchial tree and ends up in the alveoli — microscopic sacs where oxygen passes into the blood and carbon dioxide passes from the blood into the air. Click an organ.
<b>Альвеолы и газообмен.</b> Каждая альв: Alveoli and gas exchange. Each alveolus (0.2–0.3 mm) is wrapped in capillaries. The barrier between air and blood is thinner than 1 µm, and the total area of all alveoli is 70–100 m², the size of a tennis court. Oxygen (light blue) diffuses into the blood, where it is bound by the hemoglobin of red blood cells — they turn red. CO₂ (yellow) leaves into the air. The inside of the alveoli is coated with surfactant, which keeps them from sticking together.
<b>Механика дыхания.</b> Лёгкие сами не: Mechanics of breathing. The lungs do not contract by themselves: they follow the chest wall. The diaphragm descends, the ribs rise — the pressure in the lungs falls below atmospheric, and air flows in. The rhythm is set by the respiratory center of the medulla oblongata. Try the buttons on the right.
Около 20 000 вдохов в сутки. Воздух прох: About 20,000 breaths a day. Air travels down the branching bronchial tree to hundreds of millions of alveoli, where oxygen passes into the blood in a fraction of a second.
\n <div><h2>Объёмы лёгких</h2><ul>\:
Lung volumes

  • Tidal volume — ~500 mL (of which ~150 mL remains in the airways’ “dead space”).
  • Inspiratory reserve volume — ~3000 mL, expiratory reserve volume — ~1200 mL.
  • Residual volume — ~1200 mL; it cannot be exhaled.
  • VC = TV + IRV + ERV ≈ 3.5–5 L; higher in athletes.

Gas transport

Almost all oxygen is bound to the hemoglobin of red blood cells. Carbon dioxide is carried mainly as bicarbonate in the plasma.

Regulation

The respiratory center of the medulla oblongata sets the rhythm. Chemoreceptors monitor CO₂ and blood acidity: the more CO₂, the faster and deeper the breathing. You can breathe voluntarily (via the cortex), but you cannot override the center for long.

Simplifications

  • The bronchial tree is shown down to the 7th generation out of ~23.
  • Alveoli are magnified about 10,000 times.

Keys

  • 1–3 mode
  • D deep breath
  • F forced exhalation

<b>Ротовая полость.</b> Зубы измельчают: Oral cavity. The teeth grind food, and the tongue mixes it with saliva. Three pairs of salivary glands (parotid, submandibular, sublingual) secrete 1–1.5 L of saliva a day. The enzyme amylase begins to break down starch, and mucus binds the food bolus together.
The esophagus is a 25 cm muscular tube. A bolus passes through it in 5–8 seconds thanks to peristalsis — a wave of contraction of the wall. It works even upside down. At the bottom, a sphincter keeps the acidic stomach contents from flowing back (otherwise, heartburn).
<b>Желудок</b> вмещает 1–1,5 л (растягив: The stomach holds 1–1.5 L (stretching to 3–4 L). Glands in its wall secrete 2–2.5 L of gastric juice a day: hydrochloric acid (pH 1.5–2, kills microbes) and pepsin, which breaks down proteins. Mucus protects the wall from digesting itself. Food stays here for 2–4 hours and turns into semi-liquid chyme.
<b>Печень</b> — самая большая железа, ок: The liver is the largest gland, about 1.5 kg. It produces bile (up to 1 L a day), which emulsifies fats by breaking them into tiny droplets. Bile collects in the gallbladder and enters the duodenum. The liver also neutralizes toxins, stores glycogen and makes blood proteins.
<b>Поджелудочная железа</b> выделяет 1,5: The pancreas secretes 1.5–2 L of juice a day: trypsin (proteins), lipase (fats), amylase (carbohydrates) and bicarbonate, which neutralizes stomach acid. Its islets (1–2% of the tissue) are the endocrine part: insulin and glucagon.
<b>Тонкая кишка</b> длиной 4–6 м: двенад: The small intestine is 4–6 m long: the duodenum, jejunum and ileum. Here digestion is completed and almost all absorption takes place — through villi and microvilli. Food passes through it in 3–5 hours.
<b>Толстая кишка</b> (около 1,5 м): слеп: The large intestine (about 1.5 m): the cecum with the appendix, the colon (ascending, transverse, descending, sigmoid) and the rectum. It absorbs water and salts and forms feces over 12–36 hours. Trillions of bacteria of the microbiota live here: they break down fiber and synthesize vitamin K and B vitamins.
<b>Рот.</b> Пища измельчается и смачивае: Mouth. Food is ground up and moistened with saliva. Salivary amylase begins breaking down starch into maltose. The tongue shapes a bolus and pushes it into the pharynx — swallowing is triggered reflexively.
<b>Пищевод.</b> Перистальтическая волна: Esophagus. A peristaltic wave (a ring of contraction behind the bolus) pushes the food down. The lower sphincter opens and lets it into the stomach.
<b>Желудок.</b> Стенки перемешивают пищу: Stomach. The walls mix the food with hydrochloric acid and pepsin: proteins break down into peptides, microbes die. The result is acidic, semi-liquid chyme, which leaves in portions through the pylorus.
<b>Двенадцатиперстная кишка.</b> Сюда вл: Duodenum. Bile (green, breaks up fats) and pancreatic juice (trypsin, lipase, amylase, bicarbonate) pour in here. The acid is neutralized, and digestion is in full swing.
<b>Тонкая кишка.</b> Ферменты стенки зав: Small intestine. Enzymes of the wall complete the breakdown: proteins → amino acids, carbohydrates → glucose, fats → fatty acids and glycerol. They are absorbed through the villi into the blood and lymph (yellow sparks leave the intestine).
<b>Толстая кишка.</b> Непереваренные ост: Large intestine. Undigested residues (fiber) enter the cecum. Here water is absorbed (light-blue sparks), and bacteria ferment the fibers and make vitamins. The residues are compacted and expelled through the rectum.
По её стенке тянутся три мышечные ленты: Three muscular bands run along its wall (shown separately on the model) — they gather the intestine into its characteristic pouches, the haustra.
<b>Селезёнка</b> лежит слева под диафраг: The spleen lies on the left under the diaphragm, next to the stomach. It is not a digestive organ but a blood-forming and immune organ: it filters the blood and destroys old red blood cells. Its blood drains through the portal vein into the liver.
<b>Гортань и трахея</b> лежат впереди пи: The larynx and trachea lie in front of the esophagus. In the pharynx the airway and the food passage cross; during swallowing the epiglottis closes the entrance to the larynx and the larynx rises — food goes into the esophagus, not the trachea. The laryngeal cartilages (thyroid, cricoid, arytenoid) support the vocal cords.
<b>Диафрагма</b> отделяет грудную полост: The diaphragm separates the thoracic cavity from the abdominal cavity. The esophagus passes through an opening in it; the crura of the diaphragm help the lower esophageal sphincter keep acid from flowing back. If the opening is widened, part of the stomach can bulge into the chest (hiatal hernia).
<b>Скелет туловища</b> — позвоночник, рё: The skeleton of the trunk — spine, ribs, sternum, shoulder blades, pelvis — is shown for orientation. The liver, stomach and spleen are covered by the lower ribs, while most of the intestine lies lower, in and above the bowl of the pelvis.
<b>Пищеварительная система</b> — трубка: The digestive system is a tube 8–10 m long from the mouth to the anus, plus glands that secrete enzyme-containing juices into it: the salivary glands, liver and pancreas. Food is mechanically broken up, chemically split into simple molecules and absorbed into the blood. Click an organ or start the path of food.
<b>Путь пищи.</b> Комок движется по труб: Path of food. A bolus moves along the tube; the ring behind it is a wave of peristalsis. Time in the scene is compressed; the real duration of each stage is shown on the right.
<b>Ворсинки тонкой кишки.</b> Слизистая: Villi of the small intestine. The mucosa is gathered into folds, the folds are covered with villi (≈1 mm), and each villus cell carries thousands of microvilli (right). This raises the absorptive area to ~30 m². Glucose and amino acids (yellow and green) enter the blood capillaries and reach the liver via the portal vein. Fats (white) collect in a lymphatic capillary — the lacteal — and go into the lymph.
От бутерброда до глюкозы в крови — около: From a sandwich to glucose in the blood takes about a day — a journey through a tube 8–10 meters long, with acid, enzymes, bile and trillions of bacteria.
\n <div><h2>Что расщепляется и где<:
What is broken down where

  • Carbohydrates: salivary and pancreatic amylase → disaccharides → intestinal enzymes → glucose.
  • Proteins: gastric pepsin → trypsin and chymotrypsin → intestinal peptidases → amino acids.
  • Fats: bile emulsifies → lipase → fatty acids and glycerol.

Regulation

Salivation and the first phase of gastric secretion start even before eating — at the sight and smell of food (experiments of I. P. Pavlov, Nobel Prize 1904). After that, gut hormones take over: gastrin, secretin, cholecystokinin.

<b>Почки</b> — парные органы бобовидной: The kidneys are paired bean-shaped organs (10–12 cm, 150 g) on the posterior abdominal wall at the level of the T12–L2 vertebrae; the right one sits slightly lower because of the liver. About 1.2 L of blood passes through them every minute — a quarter of the heart’s total output. They cleanse the blood, keep water and salt balance and acidity constant, and secrete hormones (renin, erythropoietin).
<b>Надпочечники</b> сидят «шапочками» на: The adrenal glands sit like “caps” on the kidneys, but they are endocrine glands: the cortex secretes cortisol and aldosterone (which retains sodium and water), and the medulla secretes epinephrine and norepinephrine.
<b>Почечные артерии</b> отходят прямо от: The renal arteries branch directly off the aorta under high pressure — this is needed for filtration. The renal veins carry cleansed blood to the inferior vena cava.
The ureters are tubes 25–30 cm long. Urine moves along them not by gravity but in waves of peristalsis, in portions every 10–20 seconds.
The urinary bladder is a muscular sac. When it fills to 200–300 mL, stretch receptors send a signal to the spinal cord and cortex — and the urge appears; it holds up to 500–700 mL. Emptying is a reflex that a person learns to control from the age of 2–3 (the external sphincter is voluntary).
<b>Мочевыделительная система</b>: две по: The urinary system: two kidneys, two ureters, the urinary bladder and the urethra. The kidneys filter the blood, and urine drains into the bladder (viewed from behind — the kidneys lie against the back). Click an organ.
<b>Разрез почки.</b> Снаружи — капсула и: Kidney section. On the outside are the capsule and the cortex (where the nephron glomeruli lie). Deeper are 8–18 medullary pyramids with loops of Henle and collecting ducts; between the pyramids are the renal columns. The tips of the pyramids (papillae) open into the minor calyces → major calyces → renal pelvis → ureter. The artery enters and the vein leaves through the hilum.
<b>Нефрон</b> — рабочая единица почки, в: The nephron is the working unit of the kidney; each kidney has about a million. 1) In the glomerulus, plasma free of proteins and cells is filtered from the blood under pressure — primary urine, 150–180 L a day. 2) In the proximal tubule, all the glucose and amino acids and ~65% of the water and salts are reabsorbed (green and white sparks). 3) The loop of Henle creates a salt gradient in the medulla: the descending limb gives up water, the ascending limb gives up salt. 4) In the distal tubule and collecting duct, fine-tuning takes place under the control of hormones. What remains is 1–1.5 L of final urine.
<b>Жажда: выделяется АДГ (вазопрессин).<: Thirst: ADH (vasopressin) is released. The hypothalamus senses that the blood has become “thicker”, and the posterior pituitary releases antidiuretic hormone. Water channels — aquaporins — open in the wall of the collecting duct, and water leaves into the salty medulla (light-blue sparks). There is little urine; it is concentrated and dark.
<b>Выпили много воды: АДГ почти нет.</b>: Drank a lot of water: almost no ADH. The collecting duct becomes impermeable to water, and the water leaves with the urine. There is a lot of urine; it is dilute and pale, and the bladder fills faster.
<b>Мочеиспускание.</b> Растяжение стенки: Urination. Stretching of the bladder wall → a signal along nerves to the sacral spinal cord → contraction of the bladder muscle and relaxation of the internal sphincter. The cortex permits or forbids relaxation of the external sphincter.
Каждые сутки почки пропускают через себя: Every day the kidneys pass all of the blood through themselves about 300 times, filter out 180 liters of fluid and return 99% of it to the blood.
\n <div><h2>Что делают почки</h2><u:
What the kidneys do

  • Excrete urea, uric acid, creatinine, drugs and toxins.
  • Keep blood volume, salt concentration and pH constant.
  • Renin regulates blood pressure; erythropoietin triggers the production of red blood cells; vitamin D is activated in the kidneys.

Hormones

ADH (vasopressin) retains water, aldosterone retains sodium, and the heart’s natriuretic peptide does the opposite, removing sodium and water.

<b>Гипоталамус</b> — мост между нервной: The hypothalamus is the bridge between the nervous and endocrine systems: its neurons secrete releasing hormones. The pituitary gland (0.5 g) is the “master gland”: the anterior lobe releases tropic hormones (TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH), growth hormone and prolactin; the posterior lobe releases vasopressin and oxytocin.
ТТГ, АКТГ, СТГ, ФСГ, ЛГ, пролактин, АДГ,: TSH, ACTH, GH, FSH, LH, prolactin, ADH, oxytocin
<b>Эпифиз</b> (шишковидная железа) ночью: The pineal gland (epiphysis) secretes melatonin at night, in the dark — a “time to sleep” signal for the whole body. Light, especially blue light, suppresses its production.
<b>Щитовидная железа</b> в форме бабочки: The thyroid gland is butterfly-shaped and sits on the front of the neck. Its hormones thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3) contain iodine and set the metabolic rate in almost every cell; in children they are essential for brain development. Calcitonin lowers blood calcium.
<b>Паращитовидные железы</b> — четыре «з: The parathyroid glands are four “grains” on the back of the thyroid. Parathyroid hormone raises blood calcium: it draws calcium from the bones and retains it in the kidneys.
<b>Тимус</b> (вилочковая железа) — школа: The thymus is the school for the immune system’s T lymphocytes. It is most developed in childhood and is gradually replaced by fat after puberty.
<b>Надпочечники.</b> Кора выделяет корти: Adrenal glands. The cortex secretes cortisol (stress, blood sugar, suppression of inflammation), aldosterone (sodium and water) and small amounts of sex hormones. The medulla secretes epinephrine and norepinephrine: the “fight or flight” response within seconds.
<b>Островки Лангерганса</b> — 1–2% ткани: The islets of Langerhans make up 1–2% of pancreatic tissue — about a million cell clusters. Beta cells secrete insulin, which opens cells to glucose; alpha cells secrete glucagon, which makes the liver release glucose. Insulin deficiency causes diabetes mellitus.
<b>Половые железы</b> — яичники у женщин: The gonads are the ovaries in women (estrogens, progesterone) and the testes in men (testosterone). Their activity is controlled by pituitary FSH and LH. The hormones trigger puberty and secondary sex characteristics and affect bones, muscles and the brain.
